So shrewd an observer is Shōnagon, a lady-in-waiting to Empress Teishi, that her book’s musings on tenth-century Japanese courtly life _____ readers a thousand years later.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

accepted.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • A supercontinent is a single landmass made up of most or all of Earth’s continents.
  • Over time, continents merge together to form supercontinents, which then break apart.
  • This process is believed to take hundreds of millions of years and is known as the supercontinent cycle.
  • Ur was a supercontinent that formed about 3.1 billion years ago.
  • Columbia was a supercontinent that formed about 1.8 billion years ago.
accepted.stem: The student wants to emphasize the order in which the supercontinents were formed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The supercontinent Columbia formed long after the supercontinent Ur.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Ur formed about 3.1 billion years ago but eventually broke apart.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Forming and breaking apart over hundreds of millions of years, supercontinents are made up of most or all of Earth’s continents.

choices.label: D
choices.content: Ur and Columbia were both supercontinents, single landmasses made up of most or all of Earth’s continents.

accepted.verified: only A states the relative order (Columbia after Ur); the others give a single date, a definition, or a shared property

accepted.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Catharsis, Conversion, Traumata is a 1986 sculpture by American artist Joseph Kosuth.
  • It consists of a blue neon sign that spells out the title phrase.
  • Harvest Moon is a 2013 sculpture by British/Pakistani artist Shezad Dawood.
  • It consists of a yellow neon sign that forms an abstract moon shape.
  • Neon signs became popular with advertisers in the 1920s and began to decline in popularity in the 1960s.
  • Neon signs became popular with artists in the 1960s and continue to be popular today.
accepted.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two sculptures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Molded into an evocative phrase in Catharsis, Conversion, Traumata (1986), an abstract form in Harvest Moon (2013), and an advertising tool in decades past, neon lighting has a number of different applications.

choices.label: B
choices.content: While the sculptures share a common material, one spells out a phrase while the other is decidedly more abstract.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Kosuth’s sculpture was made in 1986 and Dawood’s in 2013, both well after the advertising heyday of neon signs had passed.

choices.label: D
choices.content: American artist Joseph Kosuth’s and British/Pakistani artist Shezad Dawood’s sculptures have employed neon signs in different ways, demonstrating the versatility of the popular material.

accepted.verified: B contrasts the two sculptures directly; A and D emphasise neon's versatility and C points out a similarity

accepted.passage: In 2015, geologist Peter Rogerson calculated that the geographic center of Kansas was a point 2.1 miles southeast of the municipality of Bushton Bend. Rogerson’s calculation was more accurate than the one from 1920 by the US Geological Survey. _____ this earlier calculation was made using far more rudimentary equipment—only cardboard and string.
accepted.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Ultimately,

choices.label: B
choices.content: Of course,

choices.label: C
choices.content: Likewise,

choices.label: D
choices.content: To that end,

accepted.verified: the second sentence gives the unsurprising reason the older calculation was less accurate; 'Of course' marks that expectedness. Source also shows B selected.

accepted.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Grimanesa Amoros is a Peruvian American artist well known for her LED light sculptures.
  • Her sculpture Uros House is made of smooth multicolored LED domes.
  • It occupies 250 cubic feet of space.
  • Her sculpture Golden Waters is made of entangled blue and white LED tubes.
  • It occupies 118,080 cubic feet of space.
accepted.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Uros House and Golden Waters. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.content: Uros House is an LED light sculpture made by Grimanesa Amoros, as is Golden Waters.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The smooth LED domes of Grimanesa Amoros’s Uros House stand in contrast to the tangled LED tubes of Golden Waters.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Grimanesa Amoros is the artist behind Uros House—a sculpture made of smooth multicolored LED domes.

choices.label: D
choices.content: At 118,080 cubic feet in size, Grimanesa Amoros’s Golden Waters cuts a larger figure than the 250-cubic-foot Uros House.

accepted.verified: only A states something both sculptures share; B and D draw contrasts and C describes one alone. Source also shows A selected.

Of course, the original ticker tape had long since been retired by the 1986 parade for the New York Mets. _____ shredded standard paper enriched the celebration.

choices.content: In other words,

choices.label: C

accepted.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Generally, an object will heat up when twisted.
  • The twisting of an object is known as torsion.
  • A 2019 study led by Zunfeng Liu and Ray Baughman tested the torsional heating of various fibers.
  • When a 0.7-millimeter-thick sample of single-ply nickel-titanium (NiTi) wire was twisted, its average surface temperature increased by 21.3°C.
  • When a 2.2-millimeter-thick sample of natural rubber fiber was twisted, its average surface temperature increased by 15.3°C.
accepted.stem: The student wants to contrast the two samples. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The natural rubber sample used in the 2019 study was thicker than the single-ply NiTi wire sample.

choices.label: B
choices.content: When the fibers were twisted as part of the 2019 study, the surface temperature of both samples increased.

choices.label: C
choices.content: Twisting an object will generally cause its temperature to increase, a process known as torsional heating.

choices.label: D
choices.content: In 2019, researchers studied the effect of torsional heating on various fibers, including samples of natural rubber and single-ply NiTi wire.

accepted.verified: only A contrasts the samples (2.2 mm vs 0.7 mm); B states a shared outcome and C and D describe the study generally

accepted.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Merle Oberon (1911–1979) was an actress born in Mumbai (then known as Bombay), India.
  • She was of Indian, Maori, and Irish heritage.
  • She was the first Indian-born actress to be nominated for an Academy Award.
  • Early in her career, she played many nameless, uncredited roles, such as her role in The Three Passions (1928).
  • Later, she played many named, credited roles, such as Marjorie Ismay in Forever and a Day (1943).
accepted.stem: The student wants to emphasize the order in which the two films were released. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The Three Passions (1928) was released early in Merle Oberon’s career, whereas Forever and a Day (1943) came out years later.

choices.label: B
choices.content: Merle Oberon was famous for her roles in films like The Three Passions (1928) and Forever and a Day (1943).

choices.label: C
choices.content: Early in her career, Merle Oberon wasn’t listed in some film credits, such as the credits for the film The Three Passions, where she played a nameless, uncredited role.

choices.label: D
choices.content: In The Three Passions (1928), actress Merle Oberon played a nameless, uncredited role; however, in Forever and a Day (1943), she played a credited role—that of Marjorie Ismay.

accepted.verified: only A frames the two films as earlier and later; the others compare credits or list them without sequence

accepted.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • A river’s stream length is the length of a line that follows along the river path.
  • A river’s valley length is the length of a straight line drawn from the beginning of the river to the end.
  • The river’s curviness, or sinuosity, is the ratio of the river’s stream length to its valley length.
  • Low-sinuosity rivers have a stream length 1–1.5 times longer than their valley length, and high-sinuosity rivers have a stream length 1.5 or more times longer than their valley length.
  • The Mississippi River in the United States has high sinuosity.
  • The Neales River in Australia has low sinuosity.
accepted.stem: The student wants to compare the curviness of the two rivers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The high-sinuosity Neales River in Australia is curvier than the low-sinuosity Mississippi River in the United States.

choices.label: B
choices.content: In both the Mississippi and the Neales rivers, curviness is determined by comparing stream length to valley length.

choices.label: C
choices.content: By comparing the stream lengths of the Mississippi and Neales rivers to their valley lengths, one can calculate their curviness, or sinuosity.

choices.label: D
choices.content: The Mississippi River’s ratio of stream length to valley length, also known as sinuosity, is greater than that of the Neales River.

accepted.verified: the notes say the Mississippi is high-sinuosity and the Neales low, so D is right and A reverses them; B and C describe the method rather than comparing

rejectedKeyConflicts.why: Choices are 'speculative, though;' / 'speculative, though,' / 'speculative; though' / 'speculative, though'. The two halves are both independent clauses, so B ('speculative, though,') is a comma splice and C leaves a fragment. A ('speculative, though;') punctuates it correctly. Rejected rather than shipped with a doubtful answer.

Transition into 'as decades passed, new calculations would reveal increasingly precise coordinates'. 'Again and again' matches the repeated-over-time sense; 'Specifically' would require the clause to specify something in the prior sentence, and it does not. Rejected.

Goal is to emphasise the discovery of (19308) 1996 TO66 to an audience ALREADY FAMILIAR with Jane Luu. The key's choice opens 'Jane Luu is an astronomer famous for...', which introduces her to an audience that does not need introducing, and frames TO66 as merely one of many. D reports that discovery specifically. Rejected.

A goal is stated ('one of their goals was for their female actor friends to have good parts to play'), then the action taken to achieve it. 'To that end' is the purpose transition; 'For example' would need the previous sentence to name a category, and it names a goal. Rejected.

'...an approach to music instruction ___ to teach music..., emphasizes retaining...'. B ('that, aiming') gives 'that, aiming to teach ..., emphasizes ...', a relative clause with a participial aside -- grammatical. The key's A ('that, is aiming') puts a comma between the relative pronoun and its verb and leaves 'emphasizes' stranded. Source also shows B selected. Rejected.

'an ecological ___ compared the lengths ... found Milvus migrans eggs to be longer'. D ('study that') makes 'that compared...' a restrictive clause and leaves 'found' as the main verb. The key's B ('study, which') opens a non-restrictive clause that is never closed, stranding 'found'. Rejected.

'Antiquarians ___ to read one of Suetonius's extant works ... might instead procure a copy'. The main verb is 'might procure', so the blank needs a participle: 'hoping'. The key's 'have hoped' is finite and gives the sentence two main verbs. Source also shows C selected. Rejected.
